speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether the Ministry will consider expanding the intake of our three local medical schools; (b) what are the measures to reduce the attrition rate of doctors in the public sector; and (c) which are the top five countries that our foreign doctors are recruited from.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: These were students whose overseas medical studies were disrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In addition, we supplement recruitment with qualified doctors from recognised universities from other countries, to ease the workload in specific departments and hospitals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We continue to make various efforts to retain our doctors within the public healthcare sector.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can MOE work with MOH to increase the intake of deserving local Polytechnic graduates?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The second supplementary question: I understand that returning Singaporeans from recognised foreign universities have a difficult path of obtaining their full registration licences.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can MOH put in measures to ease the transition?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There is a point that is related across both of the questions, which is that we have to have a series of processes that maintains standards for our medical professionals.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, on his first question, it is around the academic standards; the second is around safety and the regulatory practices around the person being fully registered.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In both cases, we have a framework looking at the standards required to enter medical school and then, to enter full practice.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We do have to make sure that the people who go into the medical schools have the aptitude, the attitude, the ability to not just complete their studies but have the ability to do well.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Having said that, there are Polytechnic graduates who are making it into medical school – we see them reported in the press.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think the importance is that they have met those standards and then, are able to flourish within medical schools; and they have a fulfilling career.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The same principle applies then to his second question, which is about foreign-trained doctors coming to practise within Singapore.
